current_definition: Wild, excessive behavior involving alcohol, pleasure, and self-indulgence carried to a harmful or shameful degree.
To slowly fall to a lower, worse, or more harmful condition than before.
A state of deep moral corruption; wicked or evil behavior that goes far beyond normal wrongdoing.
To gradually waste or spend money, energy, or resources until nothing is left.
Not allowed by law or by the rules of society; forbidden and usually done in secret.
Wrongdoing or illegal action carried out by someone in a position of official power or public trust.
Wicked and criminal in a way that is openly shocking; morally outrageous.
A deliberate act of betrayal by someone who was trusted; breaking faith with those who relied on you.
Recklessly wasteful with money or resources; also used to describe someone with no moral restraint.
To officially declare that someone is free from blame, guilt, or punishment; to release a person from an obligation or responsibility.
To make a problem, pain, or bad feeling less severe, without removing it completely.
Mercy or leniency shown toward someone who could be punished severely; a decision to reduce or forgive a penalty.
To accept or allow behaviour that most people consider wrong, either by saying nothing or by approving of it openly.
Feeling or showing deep, sincere sorrow for having done something wrong; genuinely sorry and ashamed.
Too willing to allow or forgive bad behaviour; giving people whatever they want without setting firm limits.
A small, unimportant fault or sin; a minor act of wrongdoing that people do not usually take very seriously.
Feeling sorry for doing wrong and willing to accept punishment or do whatever is needed to make things right.
Something done or paid to make up for harm or damage caused; compensation given to people who have been wronged.
To go beyond an accepted limit or rule; to do something that is morally or legally wrong.
So wrong or unfair that no reasonable person could accept it; going far beyond what is morally or legally allowable.
To warn or firmly advise someone that their behaviour is wrong, usually in a calm but serious way; to tell someone off without harsh punishment.
An official, formal statement or act declaring that someone has behaved wrongly; to issue such a statement against someone.
To criticise or punish someone harshly, especially after they have done something wrong; to scold in a forceful, sometimes harsh way.
To openly disobey or show no respect for a rule, law, or accepted standard, often in a bold or deliberate way.
An official order from a court or authority that commands someone to do something or, more often, to stop doing something.
A sharp, direct expression of disapproval given by someone in authority; to speak to someone in a way that makes clear their behaviour was wrong.
A feeling or expression of disappointment and disapproval directed at someone; to express that feeling to someone directly.
A harsh critical comment directed at a person's behaviour or work.
Gentle, kind, and unlikely to cause harm; having a pleasant and harmless effect on others.
Polite and respectful in behaviour, especially toward people one disagrees with; meeting the basic standard of good manners.
Behaving in a way that is proper, calm, and appropriate for the situation; showing good taste and self-control in conduct.
So perfect that no fault can be found; meeting the highest possible standard in every detail.
Completely harmless; unlikely to upset, offend, or cause any damage to anyone.
Very generous and forgiving, especially toward someone who has done wrong or who is in a weaker position; showing a noble, big-hearted spirit.
In perfect, original condition, with nothing damaged, spoiled, or corrupted; completely clean and unspoiled.
Producing a good or useful effect, especially by serving as a warning or lesson; beneficial even if it feels uncomfortable.
Of such outstanding quality, beauty, or greatness that it seems almost beyond what is normally possible; causing deep admiration or wonder.
Completely unwilling to change one's mind or position, no matter what arguments or pressure are applied.
So set in bad habits or a fixed way of behaving that no punishment, correction, or persuasion can bring about change.
Refusing to compromise or reach any agreement; holding a position so firmly that no middle ground is possible.
Having a habit, attitude, or way of life so deeply fixed over a long time that it is almost impossible to change.
Never stopping or letting up; continuing with full force despite difficulties, setbacks, or the passage of time.
Having a firm, clear purpose and the steady determination to carry it through, especially when facing opposition or hardship.
Strong and sturdy in body or in construction; able to withstand rough conditions without breaking down.
Loyal and committed to a person, cause, or belief in a way that does not waver even under serious pressure.
Holding on to a goal, belief, or position with great determination and refusing to let go even when the situation becomes very difficult.
The willingness to do or say something that most people would consider shockingly bold or rude; reckless daring.
A strong feeling that someone or something is far beneath you and not worth your time or respect.
Thinking only of oneself and one's own needs, interests, and views, with little or no awareness of how others feel.
Extreme admiration of oneself — one's looks, abilities, or importance — to a degree that leaves little room for genuine care about others.
